subject: Urgent: feature wedge request for MerchantLabs enterprise close
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Product Team <product@redwood.ai>, eng-leads@redwood.ai, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: feature wedge request for MerchantLabs enterprise close

Team —

Heads up: MerchantLabs told me yesterday they're ready to sign if we can ship a minimal "priority affinity" control that guarantees >95th percentile requests for a specified tenant are routed to a pre-warmed pool and get a short-lived affinity TTL (60s) that bypasses cold-starts. This is the gating ask for a $2.4M TCV deal.

What they're asking for (sales summary):
- API flag (priority=true) on requests from their tenant ID
- Routing preference to a small pre-warmed dedicated pool for those requests
- An emergency soft-rollback toggle to disable affinity if it causes degradation

I know this intersects product, serving runtime, and orchestration. I'm asking: can we scope a minimal, low-risk change we can ship as a short-lived experiment (canary) to close the deal? Key constraints from customer: cannot accept changes that add 200ms P95; they will sign a 12-month reserved capacity if we can provide an activation window and a documented rollback path.

Attachments: MerchantLabs_SOW_v2.pdf, MerchantLabs_HIPAA_QA.xlsx (they want to see the technical plan).

Asks:
1) Product/Eng: high-level viability and what the smallest ship looks like (ETA for a spike + pilot).
2) Customer Success (Monica): confirm if CS can run the pilot and own the customer rollback comms.
3) Sales (me): if we get a tentative yes by EOW Nov 25, I'll ask the customer to sign LOI and push for immediate start.

We need a real answer on risk/effort — even a prioritized backlog item with suggested timeline will help.

—Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Urgent: feature wedge request for MerchantLabs enterprise close

Steph —
Thanks for the note. MerchantLabs is high-touch: volume profile is bursty (payment reconciliation windows) and they're sensitive to tail latency; their legal team is also asking about auditability for any routing overrides.

CS can run the pilot and monitor both latency and error rates. We can also draft the rollback comms and a runbook so L2 can flip the toggle and revert routing within 5 minutes if needed.

Two operational asks:
- We need a visibility hook to see when the affinity pool is saturated (per-tenant queue depth metric).
- We need a short SLA addendum in the SOW that documents the canary window and rollback triggers.

I'll attach the customer impact appendix to the SOW in a follow-up.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Enterprise

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:49:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: feature wedge request for MerchantLabs enterprise close

Steph / Monica —

Quick read: technically feasible but with trade-offs. Some clarifying questions before we commit to an ETA: 
1) What percent of traffic do we expect to tag as priority during peak reconciliation windows? If it's >5% of global requests for sustained periods the pre-warmed pool will become expensive and will need autoscaling rules.
2) Is this per-request flag or per-session? Per-request will be easier (less state), per-session requires consistent hashing.
3) Can we accept a soft SLO degradation in routing tail while we iterate? If not, the safe path is a dedicated small pool with explicit capacity reservation (which the customer is willing to pay for).

Minimal ship idea (low risk):
- Add request header / tenant flag recognition in the routing layer (2d spike).
- Wire a routing preference to an isolated warm pool (config-only change) and expose a simple toggle in Console (4d implementation + 2d testing).
- Add a rollback API that demotes affinity and returns routing to default (1d).

End-to-end pilot: ~2 weeks (spike + small config roll + monitored pilot). That assumes Eng can allocate an engineer and SRE time for testing. If we need telemetry hooks (saturation metric), add another 2–3 days.

Risks: affinity semantics might interact with KV cache eviction (could increase cold starts elsewhere). We should scope the spike to not alter eviction policy — instead prefer capacity reservation and pre-warming.

If Sales can accept the reserved-capacity ask, that materially reduces risk and shortens the timeline.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Product Manager, Serving
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Product Team <product@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: feature wedge request for MerchantLabs enterprise close

Ben —
Appreciate the quick assessment. We can greenlight a 2-week spike + a pilot on dedicated capacity. Here's an operational compromise I propose:

1) Spike (3 business days): engineering spike to prove request header routing and a toggle. No changes to eviction policy.
2) Pilot (10 business days): enable pilot on a small dedicated pool reserved for MerchantLabs (customer pays for reserved capacity for the pilot duration).
3) Rollback: provide a Console toggle, and an incident playbook (SRE + CS) that can revert within 5 minutes.

Resource ask: we'll need one backend engineer (half-time for the spike, full-time for the pilot onboarding) and one SRE for the pilot window. If Sales secures the 12-month reserved capacity commitment in LOI, we can convert the pilot changes into a supported feature with a short roadmap slot for hardening.

Legal/Compliance: ensure the HIPAA QA doc is addressed; pass to Security to add the audit statement for routing overrides.

If Sales confirms LOI by EOD, I'll allocate the spike resources and have Eng schedule the work for next week.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Product, Platform
Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is exactly what I needed.

MerchantLabs has verbally agreed to the reserved-capacity commitment; I uploaded the signed LOI to the HubSpot record and attached the PDF here (LOI_MerchantLabs_signed.pdf). They accept the pilot constraints and will cover the pilot pool costs. They also confirmed they prefer per-request flagging (not per-session).

Next steps from Sales: I'll move to execute LOI and lock the pilot dates. Please proceed with the 3-day spike starting Monday. Monica will coordinate the pilot runbook and monitoring. Ben: please add the saturation metric to the pilot scope. Laura: I appreciate the resource allocation.

If we hit any snag on HIPAA or legal, Monica please loop Security; we need a final sign-off before we flip the pilot toggle.

—Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
